title: Duke Ellington's turn-on and Royal's banter about royalty
summary: Ellington's playful persona, his invitations to Royal and Royal's reply.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You were telling me off the tape about something that you mentioned in passing on the tape and that

was, you said that you and Duke Ellington had your own little mutual turn-on and then you gave me an example of a conversation between you and Duke, which I enjoyed very much. Want to tell me about it again?

Well, if you knew Duke Ellington, you knew that he was a turn-on artist. He enjoyed putting people on, even in his little skits that he would do in front of his band about where he would twirl his chain and talk that little jargon that he used to do about the broad on the street, whatever it was.

"Pretty and the Wolf," you know. He was always a turn-on artist. Well, he also used that as part of his psychology with the inner workings of his band. He had a whole lot of his fellows turned on because Duke was a guy that to my real feeling, I think that he actually got to the place where he accepted himself as being royalty by the name of Duke, which wasn't his real name. But I think he really got to the place where he accepted himself as being a duke and doing that, he had his serfs around him at times, his --
You were saying that Duke really thought of himself as royalty.
Yes, I was saying when the last reel went off so fast, Duke actually, I think, thought that he had

his serfs around him, which were some members of his orchestra and he controlled them so well sometimes from the manipulations of money and other things. His band was never overpaid at any time. So, he would like to turn people on. Since I'd worked with him many, many years before, he always liked to keep his position with people and he would meet me from time to time, year in, year out, and he would always come on with the heading of, "Marshal Royal, when are you going to honor me by appearing with my orchestra? I'm sure you could do so much to help improve upon the timbre of my playing and I'm sure that you would enjoy yourself over here with me. When are you going to honor me by your appearance?"

Since I didn't have to actually worry about him and I had absolutely no fear of him because he was not my employer and I owed him absolutely nothing and he owed me nothing, I always felt as though I should turn him on in the same manner and so I would turn it around and tell him, "Duke, your orchestra is just the most wonderful thing. Your expressions are something that will probably be on the archives of the world for years and years to come. I would love to play with your orchestra," which I would have, in my early days, before I actually got to know what money was all about. I would have played for him practically for free.
But at this time, I had to tell him that, "Duke, you will just have to open up your pursestrings and just give me
some of that money, so that I can go by the name that I hold, Royal, and be royalty too, by enjoying compensation for my work."
And I know he loved it.
Oh, he just loved it. He'd kiss me on each side of the cheek three times or whatever it was that he did and smile and we went on and waited until the next time.
